topics.topic_name: Elements of Food Processing and Process Design

entries.title: Bulk Density of Paddy
entries.description: Standard bulk density value used in paddy storage and bin/silo design calculations.

entries.title: Void (Air Space) of Paddy
entries.description: Standard percentage of air space within a bulk volume of paddy, used in storage capacity and aeration calculations.

entries.title: Kernel Specific Gravity of Paddy
entries.description: Standard specific gravity of an individual paddy kernel, used in grain separation and handling calculations.

entries.title: Angle of Repose of Paddy
entries.description: Standard angle of repose used when designing storage bins, hoppers, and conveying systems for paddy.

entries.title: Husk Density, Well-Packed
entries.description: Standard density of rice husk when well-packed, used in storage volume calculations.

entries.title: Husk Density, Loosely Packed
entries.description: Standard density of rice husk when loosely packed, used in storage volume calculations.

entries.title: Free Load Density of Rice Husk
entries.description: Approximate free-load (loose, unpacked) density of rice husk used in bulk handling calculations.

entries.title: Bushel to Cubic Feet Conversion
entries.description: Standard volumetric equivalence used to convert bushels to cubic feet in grain measurement.

entries.title: Standard Bushel Weight of Shelled Corn
entries.description: Government grain-standard weight defining one bushel of shelled corn at 15.5% moisture content, wet basis, used as a standard trading unit.

entries.title: Standard Height of a Stacked Paddy Bag
entries.description: Standard height of a gunny bag of paddy used in bag-storage stacking calculations.

entries.title: Standard Atmospheric Pressure
entries.description: Standard atmospheric pressure at sea level, also equal to 101.325 millibar; used as a reference value in barometric pressure and evapotranspiration calculations.

entries.title: Manning Equation Unit Conversion Factor (SI Units)
entries.description: Constant used in the Manning slope-area equation for streamflow measurement when working in SI (metric) units.

entries.title: Manning Equation Unit Conversion Factor (English Units)
entries.description: Constant used in the Manning slope-area equation for streamflow measurement when working in English (imperial) units.

entries.title: Assumed Pump Efficiency for Brake Horsepower Calculation
entries.description: Typical assumed pump efficiency value used in brake horsepower calculations for well pumps when an actual efficiency is not specified.

entries.title: Standard Allowance for Other Head Losses in Total Dynamic Head
entries.description: Standard assumed allowance, equivalent to 2 ft, added to total dynamic head calculations to account for other head losses in well pump design when a specific value is not available.

entries.title: Standard Gravitational Acceleration
entries.description: Standard value used for gravity in open channel flow computations such as the Froude number and critical flow equations; equivalent to 32.2 ft/s².

entries.title: Standard Density of Water
entries.description: Standard density of water used in soil-water volume and moisture content relationships, equivalent to 1 g/cm³, unless a location-specific value is given.

entries.title: Average Particle Density of Soil Solids
entries.description: Typical average value for the particle (mineral) density of soil solids, used in porosity and specific gravity calculations when a measured value is not provided.

entries.title: Standard Atmospheric Pressure
entries.description: Standard atmospheric pressure, equivalent to a column of 76.9 cm of mercury or 34.01 ft (10.34 m) of water; used as a reference in soil moisture tension discussions.

entries.title: Soil Moisture Tension at Permanent Wilting Point
entries.description: Standard soil moisture tension value at which plants can no longer extract water and permanently wilt; defines the permanent wilting point.

entries.title: Readily Available Moisture Fraction
entries.description: Standard fraction of the available moisture, between field capacity and permanent wilting point, considered readily extractable by plant roots; used to compute readily available moisture (RAM).

entries.title: Standard Atmospheric Pressure at Sea Level
entries.description: Atmospheric pressure exerted on a water surface at sea level; equivalent to 10,200 kgf/m² or 1 bar. Decreases above sea level and increases below it.

entries.title: Specific Weight of Water
entries.description: Standard specific weight of water used in pump suction lift and head calculations; equivalent to 0.0361 lb/in³.

entries.title: Theoretical Maximum Suction Lift
entries.description: Theoretical upper limit on suction lift set by standard atmospheric pressure acting on water, used as a ceiling when computing Net Positive Suction Head.

entries.title: Practical Suction Lift
entries.description: Practical allowable suction lift for pump installations after accounting for impurities and frictional losses; equivalent to 7.62 m. Lower than the theoretical maximum of 33 ft.

entries.title: Pump Brake Horsepower Constant (US Units)
entries.description: Conversion constant used to compute pump brake horsepower directly from flow rate in gpm and total dynamic head in feet.

entries.title: Horsepower-Hour to BTU Conversion
entries.description: Standard conversion factor between one horsepower-hour and British thermal units, used in engine energy and fuel consumption calculations.

entries.title: Horsepower to Foot-Pounds per Minute Conversion
entries.description: Standard conversion factor defining one horsepower in terms of work rate, used in engine power calculations.

entries.title: Density of Gasoline
entries.description: Standard reference density of gasoline used for fuel weight-volume conversions in engine fuel consumption problems.

topics.topic_name: Renewable and Alternative Farm Power Sources

entries.title: Solar Constant
entries.description: Fixed amount of solar energy reaching the top of Earth's atmosphere per second on one square meter facing the sun; used as the baseline value for solar power calculations.

entries.title: Typical Hydropower Plant Efficiency
entries.description: Commonly used typical energy conversion efficiency value for small-scale hydropower plant calculations.

entries.title: Total Human Power Output
entries.description: Total power a human can develop from the food energy consumed, used as a baseline for human-powered equipment calculations.

entries.title: Human Power Available for Useful Work
entries.description: Portion of a human's total power output that is available for external useful work, with the remainder used for internal body functions.

entries.title: Minimum Daily Human Energy Requirement
entries.description: Baseline minimum caloric energy requirement per day used in human power capacity calculations.

entries.title: Human Energy Conversion Efficiency
entries.description: Typical efficiency at which a human converts consumed food energy into mechanical work output.

entries.title: Mercury Barometer Altitude Conversion Factor
entries.description: Approximate change in altitude corresponding to a 1 cm change in mercury column height, used as a rough estimate in barometric leveling.

entries.title: Stadia Interval Factor
entries.description: Standard multiplying constant of a stadia-equipped telescope, used in the stadia distance formula D = Ks + C.

entries.title: Standard Subtense Bar Length
entries.description: Standard length of the subtense bar used in the subtense bar method of measuring horizontal distances.

entries.title: Coefficient of Linear Thermal Expansion of Steel (Tape Correction)
entries.description: Standard coefficient used to correct steel tape measurements for changes in temperature.

entries.title: Unit Weight of Steel (Tape Correction)
entries.description: Standard unit weight of steel used when computing sag and tension corrections for steel measuring tapes.

entries.title: Modulus of Elasticity of Steel (Tape Correction)
entries.description: Standard range of modulus of elasticity for steel used in tension-correction computations for steel measuring tapes.

topics.topic_name: Engineering Economy and Project Feasibility Analysis

entries.title: Ordinary Year (Banker's Year)
entries.description: Standard number of days per year (12 months of 30 days each) used when computing ordinary simple interest.

entries.title: Exact Year
entries.description: Actual number of days in a calendar year (366 in a leap year) used when computing exact simple interest.

entries.title: Standard Density of Water
entries.description: Standard reference density of water at 4°C, commonly used as the baseline for specific gravity calculations.

entries.title: Standard Density of Mercury
entries.description: Standard density of mercury, commonly used in manometer and pressure-measurement calculations.

entries.title: Standard Atmospheric Pressure at Sea Level
entries.description: Standard reference atmospheric pressure at sea level, also commonly expressed as 14.7 psi, 760 mmHg, or 2116 lb/ft², used for converting between gauge and absolute pressure.

entries.title: Poise to Pascal-Second Conversion
entries.description: Standard conversion factor between the poise and the SI unit of dynamic viscosity: 1 poise = 0.1 Pa·s.

entries.title: Stoke to Square Meter per Second Conversion
entries.description: Standard conversion factor between the stoke and the SI unit of kinematic viscosity: 1 stoke = 0.0001 m²/s.

entries.title: Horsepower to Watts Conversion
entries.description: Standard conversion factor between horsepower and watts, used in pump and fluid power calculations.

entries.title: Horsepower to Foot-Pounds per Second Conversion
entries.description: Standard conversion factor between horsepower and foot-pounds per second, used in fluid power calculations.

entries.title: Reynolds Number Laminar Flow Threshold
entries.description: Standard upper limit of the Reynolds number below which pipe flow is considered laminar.

entries.title: Reynolds Number Turbulent Flow Threshold
entries.description: Standard lower limit of the Reynolds number above which pipe flow is considered turbulent.
